mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 2% triggers a preemptive S&P 500 forward return correction over the next 20 trading days as market anticipates rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2.0 in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during inflation spikes (t-test p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL remains below 2% for ≥3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS exceeding 150,000 monthly suggests labor market strength that supports equity valuations, producing positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, 20-day forward returns show no significant positive deviation from the prior 60-day average (Rank IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO falling below 100) indicates weakening supply-side conditions, which typically precedes S&P 500 declines over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite INDPRO staying below 100 for ≥2 consecutive months ( walk-forward backtest).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in home sales (HOUST) above 1300 units indicates strengthening demand for durable goods, which is associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward return during confirmed demand expansion (p-value > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 4% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 exhibits negative 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate continued tightening.
failure_condition: During high FEDFUNDS periods, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% and a decline in labor force participation (implied via complement, but here using UNRATE as proxy) signals a soft landing, producing positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, cumulative 20-day forward returns are flat or negative (cumulative IC < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer demand (HOUST) below their 2020 averages simultaneously create a supply-demand imbalance, producing negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
regime_hint: dual contraction in supply and demand
failure_condition: During such dual contractions, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a post-crisis recovery regime (defined by UNRATE < 4% and FEDFUNDS < 4%), S&P 500 forward returns over 60 days tend to be positive as market anticipates stabilization.
failure_condition: In the specified regime, 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (Rank IC < 0.05).
